    9. The third lambda function combines two transformation `Obj` instances by summing their fields modulo `mod`.
    10. Reads `q` queries, each consisting of a type `t` and indices `l` and `r`.
    11. For type `t == 1`, reads an additional integer, creates an `Obj` with this integer as `a`, and applies it to the segment tree from `l` to `r`.
    12. For type `t == 2`, reads an additional integer, creates an `Obj` with this integer as `b`, and applies it to the segment tree from `l` to `r`.
    13. For type `t == 3`, computes the product of the segment tree from `l` to `r` and prints the `v` field of the result.
